subject: science
notes: Pando is a stand of quaking aspen trees in south-central Utah.
It covers about 43 hectares and contains roughly 47,000 trunks.
Genetic tests show that all of the trunks share the same DNA.
The trunks are connected by a single underground root system.
New trunks sprout from the roots rather than growing from seeds.
Pando is often described as one of the heaviest known living organisms.
stem: The student wants to emphasize Pando's size while explaining why it is considered a single organism. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Pando is considered a single organism because genetic tests show that all of its trunks share the same DNA and a single root system.
choices.B: In Pando, a stand of quaking aspen in Utah that is often described as one of the heaviest organisms, new trunks sprout from the roots.
choices.C: Spread over some 43 hectares, Pando's 47,000 or so trunks count as one organism because they share the same DNA and one root system.
choices.D: Pando, a stand of quaking aspen trees in south-central Utah, covers about 43 hectares and contains roughly 47,000 separate trunks.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: show how big Pando is and explain why it counts as one organism. The size comes from the area and trunk count; the reason comes from the shared DNA and single root system. Only one choice combines both.
explanation.A: Incorrect. It explains why Pando is one organism but says nothing about its size. This is the closest near miss because it meets the harder half of the goal.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It mentions how new trunks grow and repeats a description of Pando's weight, but it does not explain why the trunks form one organism.
explanation.C: Correct. It gives Pando's size (43 hectares, about 47,000 trunks) and the reason it is one organism (shared DNA and one root system).
explanation.D: Incorrect. It conveys Pando's size but never explains why it is considered a single organism.
